tests.covers_criterion: 1 (byte-for-byte equality; import writes no file) and 2 (gen:design-md script; running it reproduces DESIGN.md). Also the constraints that values come from the sources and that missing source content makes the generator fail.

3 (section order), 4 (colour roles and accent registry), 5 (typography, spacing, radii, control height), 6 (depth), 7 (signature components and bezel card), 8 (motion), 9 (effects), 10 (do and do-not lists), 11 (no dates or owner annotations), 12 (README row), 13 (package files list)

result.notes:
I did not run the tests because I had no shell. By reading the code, I expect every test to fail on the current code, since the generator, DESIGN.md, the npm script and the README row are all missing.

The tests require this DESIGN.md format. The CDR does not fix it.
1. **Sections:** there are nine `## ` headings, in order. Their titles match, in turn: brand or voice; colour; typography; spacing; depth; signature or component; motion; effect; and a title starting with "Do" or containing "do not" / "don't". Extra `###` headings are fine. Fenced code is ignored when headings are read.
2. **Colour roles:** use Markdown tables with Light, Dark, High contrast and Purpose (or "Use") header columns. The first cell names `--sl-<role>`.
   - **Roles:** every non-`code-*` role in `neutrals.json` `products.default` and in `tokens.themes`, plus `--sl-accent-default` (all three themes).
   - **Values:** print raw token values, including the `oklch(...)` string for light `text-on-accent`. Whitespace, backticks and case are ignored.
3. **Accent registry:** it sits in the colour section, with one line per product giving the id and both its light and dark hex. `daos` shows the resolved default accents.
4. **Token lines:** in typography, spacing and motion, one line holds both the full token name (`--sl-font-*`, `--sl-text-*`, `--sl-space-*`, `--sl-radius-*`, `--sl-motion-*`) and its full raw value. This covers every key, including `spring` and `pill`. The control height sits on a spacing-section line that also says "control" or "height".
5. **Entries:** each depth recipe, signature component and effect family has a line starting with its name. That line can be a `###` heading, list item, table row or paragraph, optionally bold, backticked or prefixed with "The". The names are:
   - **Depth:** Tile, Flat tile, Island, Key, Sunk, Float, Cast.
   - **Components:** Wordmark, Eyebrow, Tag, Inversion band, Keycap, Tile, Bezel card.
   - **Effects:** Glitch, Aurora, Glass, Goo.

   An entry runs until the next of these labels, so don't start other lines in the same section with those words. The bezel card entry must say "chosen" and "not shipped" or "not yet shipped"; no other component entry may say "not shipped". Each effect entry contains its meaning phrase from the "X means *...*" sentence in design-language.md.
6. **Motion rules:** the section mentions reduced motion, page-load choreography and the dither.
7. **Do lists:** the last section has `### Do` and `### Do not` headings (`##` to `####` are accepted; "Don't" and a trailing "list" also work). A `## Do ...` heading must also serve as the ninth section's start. The do-not list contains each flavour.md trait name word for word. The do list keeps the key words of all 12 brand traits.
8. **No history:** the output has no ISO dates, "owner ruling/amendment/decision/override/approval/pick", "(owner", "owner," or "owner:", "amended" or "amendment", or "until/since [ui-kit] X.Y". This also applies to quoted flavour.md rule cells.
9. **README row:** it has the form ``| `DESIGN.md` | description |``.

The generator tests run on a temporary copy containing only `package.json`, `sondalab.tokens.json`, `docs/`, `scripts/` and `packages/ui-kit/`, so the generator must not read anything outside these.
- **Source changes:** the tests change some space, radius, text and motion tokens. They replace every `32px` with `36px` in both copies of design-language.md, and add a new flavour.md do-not row. All of these must show up in the output without an error, so don't require a hand-written entry for each do-not trait, and don't pin 32 anywhere.
- **Broken sources:** the script must exit non-zero and leave DESIGN.md untouched if every `32px` is gone, the do-not-converge section is gone, or `shared.motion` is gone.
- **Run-directly check:** `buildDesignMd()` must return a string synchronously for the byte-for-byte test.

The tests don't check the wording of the brand summary or of the reasons beside rules, or which source wins when flavour.md and design-language.md disagree, so review those by hand.

assumptions: No shell was available, so I could not run the generator or the tests. I worked out the generator's output by hand and wrote the committed DESIGN.md to match it exactly. I cross-checked every source value, the key order (integer-like keys in `space` sort numerically, which matches the file) and the joining of sections with a blank line and a single trailing newline.

The light and dark neutrals in the colour table are the default product's, taken from the generated `neutrals.json` (`products.default`), as both the CDR and the frozen test specify. High contrast uses `themes.high-contrast`.

The do-list items are flavour.md's traits shown verbatim with their design-language citation ("See L3 Wordmark."). The do-not items are the trait plus its current rule, with the owner attribution and date removed.

Writing rule prose that names a fixed fact of a rule, such as the 1px hairline or the 8x8 Bayer matrix, does not count as typing a token value. Token values and the control height always come from the sources.
risks: The byte-for-byte test depends on my hand-built DESIGN.md matching the generator's output exactly, because nothing could be run here. If it fails, running `npm run gen:design-md` once rewrites the file to match.

The generator fails on purpose when a new colour role, radius, font role or motion token is added to the sources without a written use. A later token change therefore needs a one-line use added in `gen-design-md.mjs`, otherwise `gen:tokens` (which now runs the generator) stops.

I could not search the repository. Another existing test may enumerate `agent/` files, `package.json` scripts or colour literals in shipped markdown, and react to the new file or the extended `gen:tokens` chain.
If flavour.md ever switches to CRLF line endings, the bezel bullets would keep a trailing carriage return. Table cells are trimmed, so they would not.

follow_ups.why: Without a shell I could not run the full suite. Something like a parity check on shipped agent docs, or a colour-literal scan of agent/*.md, might need to know about DESIGN.md.

learnings: gen-design-md.mjs requires a written use for every colour role, radius, font role and motion token, and fails on any new token without one.
flavour.md do-not rows carry 'Owner decision, <date>:' prefixes; gen-design-md strips them and must keep the output free of dates and owner notes.
The design-language control height is read from the phrase 'are all **32px**'; rewording that sentence breaks gen-design-md and its frozen test.

payload.head: f352aa888a1bdbff7d5e4edbf2664bc06073e7e1
payload.requirement: Constraint: values come from the sources at build time and are never typed into the generator, including values that exist only in prose.
payload.description: Only the control height and the four effect meanings are read from prose. Other prose values are typed into scripts/gen-design-md.mjs, for example the '8x8 Bayer threshold', the seam's '3:1' and the '1px' widths. If design-language.md changes one of them, the generator neither follows nor fails, so DESIGN.md goes stale without any sign. The test below uses the Bayer matrix size as its example.
payload.evidence: motion() has the literal 'a fill that grows through an 8x8 Bayer threshold'. docs/design-language.md L4, 'The hover is a dither wipe', is where that value is stated. components() has the literal 'the seam carries the state at 3:1'.

payload.head: f352aa888a1bdbff7d5e4edbf2664bc06073e7e1
payload.requirement: Constraint: if source content the generator relies on is missing, it fails instead of silently writing an empty or stale value.
payload.description: accentRows() reads accents through need(), which only checks that the key exists. An empty string or null for a non-default product's accent builds without error. The accent registry table then gets an empty cell or `null`. The depth and fill values go through the same check.
payload.evidence: In scripts/gen-design-md.mjs, need() tests only `key in value`. accentRows() passes its result straight to code(). colourRoles() and scale() reject empty values, but this path does not.

payload.head: f352aa888a1bdbff7d5e4edbf2664bc06073e7e1
payload.requirement: Constraint: if source content the generator relies on is missing, it fails instead of silently writing a stale value (the bezel card's chosen-not-shipped status).
payload.description: The generator hard-codes 'Bezel card — chosen, not yet shipped'. It finds the flavour.md section with /bezel card/i only and never reads the status. After flavour.md marks the card as shipped, the build still succeeds and tells design agents not to use it.
payload.evidence: components() calls flavourSection(src.flavour, /bezel card/i) and then writes the literal status line. The source of that status is the flavour.md heading '## 2 — The bezel card (chosen, not yet shipped)' and the paragraph below it.

payload.head: f352aa888a1bdbff7d5e4edbf2664bc06073e7e1
payload.requirement: Constraint: keep each rule's reason beside it in one short sentence.
payload.description: Several rules in DESIGN.md have no reason. None of the 12 Do items has one; each ends only in a 'See L…' pointer. Most Do-not items give the name of the broken rule instead of a reason, for example 'L1: five roles, fixed pairing.' The four effect-family meaning bullets and several depth and signature rules are also uneven on this. An agent that reads only this file does not learn why those rules exist.
payload.evidence: packages/ui-kit/agent/DESIGN.md §9 has lines such as '- Pixel check, radio and switch. See L4 Pixel controls.'. dos() builds each Do line as `- ${trait} See ${source}.`.

payload.head: f352aa888a1bdbff7d5e4edbf2664bc06073e7e1
payload.requirement: Constraint: where flavour.md and design-language.md disagree, design-language.md wins; state each rule in its current form.
payload.description: DESIGN.md §8 says without qualification that a disabled control is greyed by a 1px checker mask. design-language.md L6 makes exceptions: the slider keeps half opacity, high contrast and forced colours keep half opacity, and a busy aurora control stays unmasked. A design agent following DESIGN.md would mask sliders and busy controls.
payload.evidence: docs/design-language.md:200 says 'High contrast and forced colours keep the half opacity ... a busy aurora control stays unmasked ... The slider keeps half opacity.' effects() in the generator leaves all of these out.

findings.requirement: Constraint: where sources disagree, design-language.md wins. The colour section must give each colour role its correct purpose. Under design-language.md Decision 2, text and thin lines use the --slc-accent-text reading, not the fill.
findings.description: The `--sl-accent-default` row of DESIGN.md assigns this token to the focus ring, links and tags. On light, its value is the fill (#FF9F1C). The shipped focus ring is `--slc-focus` = `var(--sl-focus-ring, var(--slc-accent-text))`, and light.css caps `--sl-focus-ring` at lightness 0.46. Links and tag text are accent text, which has the same cap. DESIGN.md never names `--sl-focus-ring`. An agent that follows the table would draw a bright orange focus ring and orange text on the light canvas, which is too faint to read. This also conflicts with the file's own 'Fill and text are one accent, two readings' bullet. The wording is typed into COLOUR_USE in the generator.
findings.evidence: scripts/gen-design-md.mjs COLOUR_USE['accent-default']: 'The product accent: primary fill, focus ring, links, tags, the seam.' docs/design-language.md:49: '--slc-accent is the colour a control fills with. --slc-accent-text is the same hue as text or a thin line'. packages/ui-kit/components.css:193: --slc-focus: var(--sl-focus-ring, var(--slc-accent-text)). packages/ui-kit/themes/light.css:27: --sl-focus-ring is capped with min(l, var(--sl-accent-text-lmax)).

findings.requirement: Intent: DESIGN.md lets design agents scaffold on-system UI, including the per-product accent registry.
findings.description: The accent registry text tells a non-default product to load themes/products.css and set data-sl-product, but never says how to apply the accent. products.css sets only the neutrals, code neutrals and any registered fill, not `--sl-accent-default`. An agent following these steps for spexr or introspect would get that product's tinted neutrals with the default amber accent. DESIGN.md should say that the product also overrides `--sl-accent-default` with its registry value for each theme.
findings.evidence: The text under '### Accent registry' in DESIGN.md mentions only products.css and data-sl-product. The header of packages/ui-kit/themes/products.css says it holds each product's neutrals and its registered fill. The product blocks shown there declare no --sl-accent-default.
